title: DHIS2 export reads the wrong Bikram Sambat month when month_start_date is not 1
research_next_step: Map existing DHIS2 reporting-period tests to the observed writer/exporter mismatch and prepare concrete boundary examples for a maintainer scope question; do not choose reporting semantics on the maintainer's behalf.
problem: CHT issue #11342 reports that with Bikram Sambat reporting months enabled and month_start_date not equal to 1, DHIS2 target export can read an adjacent target month or zero because the export key derives from the raw selected date rather than the reporting interval used by target writers.
humanitarian_relevance: Target exports can feed health program reporting and supervision workflows. Incorrect month aggregation could misstate operational performance for Nepali-language deployments, but Humanifest should not overclaim patient outcome impact from this issue alone.

evidence.claim: Issue author reports a local 5.2.0 reproduction where an August 2026 export returned the BS 2083-04 total rather than the stored 2083-05 total.

Read-only source inspection confirmed api/src/services/export/dhis.js targetDocsInMonth builds the BS key from moment(timestamp), while webapp and rules-engine paths use interval end dates for target tags.
On 2026-09-08, read-only GitHub issue metadata reported OPEN, no assignees, 0 comments, and updatedAt 2026-08-26T10:20:43Z. This does not establish maintainer availability or reproducibility.

At the inspected commit, api/tests/mocha/services/export/dhis.spec.js contains Bikram Sambat export coverage with an explicit month_start_date of 1; no non-default month_start_date case was found in that file. Tests were read, not executed.
At the inspected commit, targetDocsInMonth derives the Bikram Sambat lookup month from moment(timestamp), and the caller passes the selected from date.

code_surface: medic/cht-core: api/src/services/export/dhis.js and API DHIS tests; shared-libs/calendar-interval, rules-engine provider-wireup, webapp UHC settings, and admin export-dhis controller/tests. Inspected committed source at 35b2bb6dac0844bee3228476591d08d56c5dd10d; final implementation scope awaits maintainer agreement.
proposed_change: After maintainer confirmation, agree the meaning of from, picker labels, and exported period before selecting the smallest coherent fix. Align target-doc lookup with writer interval semantics and existing start-day setting precedence; a backend-only lookup change must not be assumed to resolve the full issue.
tests: After scope confirmation, test distinct adjacent-month totals, both sides of a non-default reporting boundary, default-day controls, Gregorian compatibility, setting precedence, and year/month transitions. Vary the admin clock for the same displayed period and assert the agreed from and payload period semantics. API and admin test surfaces are located; no target tests were added or run. See research/2026-09-08-cht-dhis-period-audit.md.
environment: Tier 1 for source inspection; Tier 3 Codespaces/devcontainer recommended before implementation because cht-core is large and uses multiple package workspaces, CouchDB-related services, and project-controlled npm scripts.
maintainer: No current maintainer confirmation or assignee. A future authorized inquiry should settle the reporting-period contract (from, picker, payload label), not assume interval-derived lookup alone closes the issue.
risks: Medium: current admin month labels preserve a day-dependent timestamp, so a containing-interval lookup alone may select different reporting periods for the same displayed month on different visit dates. This is a source-derived risk, not an executed reproduction. Picker semantics, output labels, and Gregorian compatibility require an agreed scope.
